findings.title: Each retry mints a new message_id, so a retry after a lost reply pays the transfer twice
findings.trigger: transfer_message is called inside the retry loop, and transfer_message (messages.py) sets message_id from new_message_id(), a fresh uuid4 on every call. When an attempt is applied but its reply is lost (GatewayTimeout, or a 504 from the gateway), the next attempt carries a different message_id.
findings.impact: The gateway deduplicates only on message_id, so it applies the retried message as a new transfer: the recipient is paid twice. The comment and PR description claim the opposite. Build the message once before the loop so every attempt sends the same message_id.
